- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then overshoot, followed by a sharp drop — suggesting overreaction to recent spikes.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts drift downward after initial spikes, but often overshoot the true mean by 5–10%.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility clustering; underestimates sharp drops after spikes.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices — model overweights recent trends.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of corrections after spikes — true outcomes often drop more sharply than forecasted.
- Forecasts should be scaled down by 5–10% in early periods and adjusted downward by 2–3% per day after peak to reflect mean reversion.
- Model overfits to recent high prices; should apply smoothing or decay factor to reduce influence of last 5–7 days.
